text:
Jordan: [incident-bot] PAGED: gpu-health-high-ecc-counts — multiple ECC corrections on nvidia-node-72, thermal spikes, progressive node drains. Paging team: @eng-oncall
incident-bot: alert triggered 2026-02-15T03:12:05Z — p99 inference latency up 3x on rtx-cluster, VRAM fragmentation alarms on 72/73, automatic drain started on pool-prod-gpu.
Alex: I'm on it. pulling logs now. any customer-facing impact reported?
Marina: saw a couple of 502s from model-serving in eu-west-1, small spike ~2m, appears correlated with node drains
Samir: adding node-level metrics: ECC corrections, board temp, power cap. starting a manual drain hold on 72 to keep jobs from bouncing: `kubectl annotate node nvidia-node-72 oncall/drain-hold=true` :hammer_and_wrench:
Alex: good call. I'm isolating noisy pods. running `rg -n "OOM|vram" /var/log/nvidia` to find patterns
incident-bot: auto-silenced alert route gpu-health-noise for 15m per transient rule (reason: correlated with hardware ECC bursts). see /alerts/3772
Marina: echoing — customers A and B hit transient failures. PG ticket created: PG-6884. Not widespread but taking it seriously.
Samir: short-term mitigations applied: 1) hold drains on bad nodes 2) move long-running batches off the cluster 3) set eviction threshold higher for vram fragmentation for 10m
Jordan: can we tweak alerting to reduce noise? current ECC burst flashes are causing repeated pagers. propose: change ECC corrections alert from count>=5/1m to count>=20/5m and add a dedupe window of 10m. also add explicit VRAM fragmentation metric `vram_frag_ratio > 0.85` for 3m.
Alex: agreed. also add debounce on thermal spike alert: require 2 consecutive 30s samples above threshold before page.
Marina: I'll make dashboard changes. New panels: ECC corrections heatmap, VRAM fragmentation per device, drain-rate by pool. Anyone object to adding a 'noisy-node' label in grafana for quick filtering?
Samir: +1. That'll help triage. we'll need a small playbook change: on noisy-node label set, don't auto-drain for 20m and run diagnostics first.
Jordan: Marina — drop the grafana link here when done. Also file an infra task for longer-term: test kernel/fwr update on a canary node.
Marina: pushing dashboard now — panels created, snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/8c2e/gpu-health-snapshot?orgId=1 (:eyes:)
Marina: updated alert rule — `gpu.ecc.corrections.count` changed to `sum_over_time(...) >= 20` with `for: 5m`, dedupe=600s. rule id 8722. applied to prod: `kubectl apply -f /k8s/alerts/gpu-ecc.yaml`
Alex: thanks. I'll monitor paging noise. setting a temporary pager route that pages only on `for: 10m` persistent >= threshold. issuing: `ops-bot silence --route gpu-health:10m --reason "post-incident debounce"`
ops-bot: route gpu-health silenced for 10m by alex
Samir: noticed VRAM fragmentation alerts often follow high-memory churn from beam search workloads. we should add model-tagged routing so heavy-batch workloads can be scheduled on nodes with lower fragmentation risk.
Jordan: agreed as long-term. short-term, reduce pack count for heavy models by default to reduce churn. created ticket INFRA-10221 for scheduler change.
Marina: customer impact note: PG-6884 updated — 2 customers impacted for 2-3m, no data loss, autoscaling partially contributed. flagged for SRE postmortem.
Jordan: handoff to night shift: @samir you own next 4h, will be reachable via DM. summary: temporary alert debounce applied, hold on auto-drain, dashboards updated, PG-6884 created, INFRA-10221 created, kernel canary scheduled. see runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/GPU+Node+Health+Runbook
Samir: taking handoff. will keep an eye on ECC traces and VRAM fragmentation. will escalate if ECC corrections continue after dedupe window.
Alex: quick note — we've also added a scraping change to expose `vram_frag_ratio` on exporter `nvidia-metrics-exporter` at /metrics.v2
Marina: post-incident tasks (short list): - validate kernel on canary node - run synthetic workload to reproduce fragmentation - add model-tag routing to scheduler - review pack defaults - schedule postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 PST
Jordan: assigning owners: canary kernel = @alex, synthetic workload = @marina, scheduler ticket = @samir, pack defaults = @jordan
Samir: logging handoff: `thread_ts=2260001111 handoff by jordan at 2026-02-15T04:05Z` — will post updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
Alex: monitoring looks quiet now, p99 latency trending down. will keep silence until end of window.
incident-bot: auto-update: alerts reduced by 72% after debounce rule; next review in 24h. Incident severity: sev2 -> monitoring. CI jobs: none affected.
Marina: scheduling postmortem doc in confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=54321
Jordan: thanks everyone. follow-ups: add alert dedupe explanations to oncall playbook, review default alert windows across GPU alerts, and add a customer impact summary to PG-6884. closing handoff.
Samir: leaving a final note: if we're still seeing noisy nodes after kernel canary, plan is to RMA hardware. will escalate to hw-eng if needed.
Alex: :thumbsup:
Marina: :pray:
ops-bot: incident closed for pager gpu-health-high-ecc-counts — silence window ended.
